tour.overview:
Four thousand years ago, Crete was home to Europe's first great civilisation. The Minoans, named after the mythical King Minos, built palaces of hundreds of rooms, painted their walls with dolphins, lilies and young men leaping over bulls, and traded across the Mediterranean. The largest palace, Knossos, with its maze of corridors, may have given rise to the legend of the Labyrinth and the Minotaur. Excavated and partly reconstructed by Arthur Evans from 1900, it is the most visited site on the island.

This private day explains Minoan Crete with a licensed archaeologist guide. You visit Knossos in the morning, before the heat, then see its treasures – the original frescoes, the snake goddesses, the Phaistos Disc – in the Heraklion Archaeological Museum, one of the great museums of the world. After a walk to the Venetian harbour, you drive into the hills for lunch in a village with a tasting of Cretan olive oil and raki.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 7 hours 30 minutes
• Start and end: your hotel in Heraklion or on the north coast, or the cruise port
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy; about 4 km, with uneven ground and steps at Knossos

WHAT YOU SEE
• The palace of Knossos: the throne room, the grand staircase, the royal apartments and the storerooms.
• The Heraklion Archaeological Museum.
• Heraklion: the Venetian harbour, the Koules fortress, the Morosini fountain and the Venetian walls.
• A village in the hills, such as Archanes.

WHY THIS WORKS
We start at Knossos at opening time to beat the heat and the cruise groups, and see the museum afterwards, when the palace makes sense of what you see in the glass cases.

WHO IT SUITS
History and mythology lovers, families, and cruise passengers in Heraklion.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer nature, ask us about the Samaria Gorge or the beaches of Balos and Elafonisi in western Crete.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Knossos has little shade: bring a hat and water. Parts of the palace were reconstructed in concrete by Evans; your guide explains what is original. The museum is closed on some public holidays.

days.name: The palace of Knossos, the Heraklion Archaeological Museum, the Venetian harbour and lunch in a Cretan village
days.description:
What to expect: the Minoan civilisation and the island's Venetian past, with a licensed guide, private car, tickets and a village lunch.

Your driver collects you at your hotel or at the cruise port at about 7:45 and drives to Knossos, 5 kilometres south of Heraklion, for the opening. Your guide leads you through the palace, first built around 1900 BC, destroyed by earthquakes and rebuilt, and finally abandoned after about 1350 BC. You see the West Court and its storage pits, the long corridors of storerooms with giant clay jars, pithoi, as tall as a person, and the throne room with its gypsum throne, perhaps the oldest in Europe, flanked by painted griffins. You walk down the Grand Staircase, five flights built around a light well, into the royal apartments with the Queen's Megaron and its dolphin fresco, and see the first flushing toilet and the clay water pipes. Your guide explains how Arthur Evans reconstructed parts of the palace in concrete and painted copies of the frescoes, and why archaeologists still debate it.

Back in Heraklion, you visit the Archaeological Museum, home to almost all the great Minoan finds. You see the snake goddesses, the bull's-head rhyton carved in black stone, the Phaistos Disc with its spiral of stamped signs still undeciphered, the gold bee pendant of Malia, and upstairs the original frescoes from Knossos: the Prince of the Lilies, the Ladies in Blue and the bull-leaping scene.

After a walk through the centre to the Morosini fountain, with its four lions, and the Venetian harbour guarded by the Koules fortress, built by Venice in the 16th century, you drive 20 minutes into the hills to a village such as Archanes, surrounded by vineyards and olive groves. Lunch is at a family taverna – dakos, slow-cooked lamb, snails, local cheese and greens – with a tasting of Cretan extra virgin olive oil and raki. You are back at your hotel or ship at about 15:15.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:45 – Pick-up at your hotel or the port.
08:00 – Palace of Knossos (about 2 hours).
10:30 – Heraklion Archaeological Museum (about 1 hour 30 minutes).
12:15 – Morosini fountain, Venetian harbour and the Koules.
13:15 – Lunch and tasting in a village.
15:15 – Back at your hotel or ship.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Cruise passengers: we plan to have you back at least one hour before all-aboard time.
• The Koules fortress interior can be added.
• The tomb of Nikos Kazantzakis, author of Zorba the Greek, on the Venetian walls, can be included.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, Knossos and museum tickets, lunch with tasting, bottled water, pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: Koules fortress, extra drinks, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Can you pick us up from the cruise ship?
faq.answer: Yes. Knossos is 15 minutes from the cruise terminal of Heraklion, and we plan the day around your ship's times.

faq.question: We are staying far from Heraklion. Can we join?
faq.answer: Yes, from anywhere on the north coast. From Chania or Rethymno, the drive adds about 1 to 2 hours each way; we quote it with your request.

faq.question: Are the entrance tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes: Knossos and the Heraklion Archaeological Museum.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, lunch at a village taverna with olive oil and raki tasting. Vegetarian and other diets can be arranged.

faq.question: Is there much walking?
faq.answer: About 4 km. Knossos has uneven ground, steps and some slopes; the museum is easy.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the labyrinth, the Minotaur story and the frescoes of dolphins and bulls. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. Knossos has an accessible route around part of the site; the museum is fully accessible. Tell us your needs.

faq.question: Is everything at Knossos original?
faq.answer: No. Arthur Evans reconstructed parts of the palace in concrete and placed painted copies of frescoes; the originals are in the museum. Your guide explains what is ancient and what is modern.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops. Buying olive oil at the village is optional.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes, a hat and sun cream. Knossos has little shade.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: April to June and September to October. Summer is hot; we start at opening time. Winter is mild and quiet.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
